TITLE HISTORY, from the title page and new here: this is a 'Revision of title "Collatz Conjecture: Propositions derived from Parity Vector Analysis"'. THE PAPER B OPEN RISK IS CLOSED AND THE ANSWER IS NO. The body contains NO ASYMPTOTIC of any kind: no growth constant, no power of the length, no oscillation, no prefactor. A full-text search for asymptotic vocabulary over all 58000 characters returns one hit, and it is the elementary drift identity log(S_k) = log(S_0) + d(k) log 3 - k log 2. It never names the OEIS sequences either -- A076227, A100982 and A260591 have ZERO occurrences -- so even the identification of these counts with OEIS entries is not January's; that arrives with Winkler's Remark and with Hikawa's July and September texts. SCOPE OF THAT CLAIM: it is a full-text search for asymptotic vocabulary and for the OEIS ids against a body whose every numbered result sits in a generation-and-counting frame, not a line-by-line reading of all 29 pages. WHAT IT ACTUALLY CONTAINS. Lemmas 1-11 with Theorems 1, 2 and 4; classification of finite-length parity vectors into J-converged, A-converged and U-converged by Terras's convergence condition; counting by length and by number of 1s; ALGORITHM 2, which generates the weight-(d+1) unconverged and just-converged vectors from the weight-d ones by appending a 1 and then 0s, testing convergence with k > d log 3 / log 2 -- our ceiling condition written as a generation rule; the Bird's eye view visualisation; and a closing list of empirical hypotheses supporting the affirmative conjecture. PRIOR-ART CONSEQUENCE. The clock splits. The COUNTING OBJECTS do start here, January 2026, six months before the toolkit, as this register already said. The ASYMPTOTIC LAYER does not: it starts with July's Theorem 6.3 and Conjecture 7.1. The oscillation and the prefactor appear in none of the three papers of the line. CO-AUTHOR: Kazuo Nakanishi, who appears nowhere else in our records and must not be dropped from a citation. BIBLIOGRAPHY, and two of its entries were missing here: winkler-2015-stopping-time-behavior (reference [4]) and kay-2021-characteristic-zero-one-strings (reference [6]); the abstract names Terras, Roosendaal and Kay as the paper's three foundations. Reference [1] is the matwbn Terras URL; [2]-[3] are Roosendaal's pages, which is where 'glide' comes from. The toolkit is a declared supplement to this paper (Zenodo relatedIdentifiers, isSupplementTo). Paper B's reference 10 cites it since the 20 September evening edition, from the July paper's secondhand description; that citation can now be made from the text.
